served.stem: Three protonated nitrogen acids are compared: methylammonium (CH3NH3+, shown), anilinium (C6H5NH3+), and pyridinium (C5H5NH+). Which is the strongest acid (lowest pKa), reflecting the WEAKEST/most-stabilized conjugate base?
choices: All three have identical pKa because each loses an N-H proton
Anilinium; its conjugate base aniline has the N lone pair delocalized into the benzene ring, making aniline a weak base and anilinium the strongest acid
Methylammonium; a primary amine cation is always the most acidic
Pyridinium; the aromatic ring feeds electron density to nitrogen and makes pyridine a stronger base than methylamine
Methylammonium; the alkyl group's electron donation makes methylamine the weakest base of the three, which leaves its cation as the strongest acid of the set by a wide margin
served.bankWhy: Aniline is the weakest base (N lone pair delocalized into the ring), so its conjugate acid anilinium (pKa ~4.6) is the strongest acid, below pyridinium (~5.2) and methylammonium (~10.6).

answer.text: Anilinium; its conjugate base aniline has the N lone pair delocalized into the benzene ring, making aniline a weak base and anilinium the strongest acid
answer.line: Judge each acid by its base. Aniline's lone pair spreads into the ring, so aniline is the weakest base and anilinium the strongest acid.

steps: Turn each acid into its base by taking off the N-H proton: aniline, pyridine and methylamine.
Rank the bases. Aniline's lone pair spreads into the ring, so it is the weakest. Pyridine's sp2 pair is held close to N. Methylamine's pair sits free, pushed by a methyl.
Weakest base, strongest acid. Anilinium, about 4.6, edges out pyridinium, about 5.2; methylammonium, about 10.6, is the weakest acid of the three.

choices.text: All three have identical pKa because each loses an N-H proton
choices.note: The proton is the same, but what is left behind is not. The three bases hold their lone pairs very differently.

choices.text: Anilinium; its conjugate base aniline has the N lone pair delocalized into the benzene ring, making aniline a weak base and anilinium the strongest acid
choices.note: The ring soaks up aniline's lone pair, so anilinium lets its proton go most easily.

choices.text: Methylammonium; a primary amine cation is always the most acidic
choices.note: Methylammonium is the weakest acid here, because methylamine, with its lone pair free, is the strongest base.

choices.text: Pyridinium; the aromatic ring feeds electron density to nitrogen and makes pyridine a stronger base than methylamine
choices.note: Pyridinium, about 5.2, really is close. But its reason runs backward: pyridine is a much weaker base than methylamine, not a stronger one.

choices.text: Methylammonium; the alkyl group's electron donation makes methylamine the weakest base of the three, which leaves its cation as the strongest acid of the set by a wide margin
choices.note: Alkyl groups do donate electron density. That makes methylamine the strongest base here, so its cation is the weakest acid.
